CERT-EU.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
CERT-EU.description:
On 20 October 2026, the PHP project announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP. Public reports indicated that these vulnerabilities could lead to remote code execution (RCE).
The PHP team released the fixes today, 21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC, in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Both vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Technical details are now being discussed publicly, and initial proofs of concept (PoCs) have begun to circulate. This raises the likelihood that attackers are already exploiting the vulnerabilities.
[New] On 23 October, PHP disclosed a new RCE vulnerability. However, it affects only web applications configured in an unusual way, and PHP considers it an unlikely risk. PHP will not issue an out-of-band release for this vulnerability. Instead, organisations are advised to apply mitigation to fully protect from this RCE vector.
CERT-EU advises organisations to patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
CERT-EU.description:
On 21 October 2026, GitLab published a security advisory addressing several vulnerabilities among which a critical flaw that could allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on a GitLab server.
CERT-EU recommends organisations to update affected assets as soon as possible, prioritising internet facing assets, and to run an assessment to identify compromised assets.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
CERT-EU.description:
On 14 October 2026, Cisco published a security advisory addressing a critical vulnerability affecting the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway. This vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system.
The Cisco PSIRT is aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability.
CERT-EU strongly recommends updating the Content Scanner Tools package or upgrading Cisco AsyncOS Software to a fixed release as soon as possible, prioritising appliances reachable from the internet. CERT-EU also recommends checking all affected appliances for indicators of compromise.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-016: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab CE and EE
CERT-EU.description:
On 12 October 2026, GitLab released versions 19.4.2, 19.3.4 and 19.2.8 of GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE), fixing 24 security issues among which a critical vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server.
CERT-EU strongly recommends upgrading self-managed GitLab CE/EE instances to a fixed version as soon as possible, starting with internet-facing instances.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-015: Critical Vulnerability in Multiple Atlassian Products
CERT-EU.description:
On 5 October 2026, Atlassian published a security advisory addressing a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability. It affects Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center, Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye.
CERT-EU strongly recommends upgrading all affected installations to a fixed version as soon as possible, starting with instances accessible from the internet. CERT-EU also recommends checking access logs for signs of exploitation.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
CERT-EU.description:
On 27 September 2026, Citrix published a security bulletin addressing 8 vulnerabilities affecting customer-managed Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway, among which 2 critical unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities. Citrix has confirmed active exploitation of these 2 critical vulnerabilities in the wild.
CERT-EU recommends updating affected software and running a compromise assessment on those exposed on the internet.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
CERT-EU.description:
On 22 September 2026, F5 published an advisory addressing a critical vulnerability affecting its BIG-IP APM product. The vendor confirmed active exploitation in the wild.
CERT-EU recommends taking appropriate actions as soon as possible.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
CERT-EU.description:
On 9 September 2026, Check Point released emergency security updates addressing two critical vulnerabilities affecting Check Point Security Gateway, Security Management Server, and Spark Firewall deployments configured to use Remote Access VPN or Site-to-Site VPN. Both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS score of 9.8 and could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on affected appliances.
CERT-EU strongly recommends applying the available hotfixes as soon as possible, prioritising internet-facing and perimeter appliances.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-011: Critical Vulnerabilities in SAP Kernel and NetWeaver Message Server
CERT-EU.description:
On 8 September 2026, as part of its September Security Patch Day, SAP released Security Notes addressing two critical vulnerabilities affecting a broad range of SAP products[3]. The most severe, CVE-2026-44756 (CVSS 10.0), is a memory corruption vulnerability in SAP Extended Passport (EPP) processing, nicknamed "OVERPASS" by the Onapsis Research Labs (ORL), which discovered and responsibly disclosed it[3]. The second, CVE-2026-58240 (CVSS 9.8), nicknamed "S4GET", is a missing authentication check in the SAP NetWeaver Message Server[6].
Both are remotely exploitable without authentication. According to the reporting researchers, successful exploitation of either can result in arbitrary operating system command execution under the account that owns the SAP installation, leading to full compromise of the affected system and the business data it holds[6].
CERT-EU strongly recommends applying SAP Security Notes 3747649 and 3759472 as soon as possible.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-010: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
CERT-EU.description:
On 19 August 2026, Citrix published a security advisory addressing multiple critical vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC (formerly Citrix ADC) and NetScaler Gateway (formerly Citrix Gateway).
CERT-EU recommends updating affected devices as soon as possible.

Canadian Cyber Centre.title: AL26-028 – Ongoing Help Desk Voice Phishing Campaign Targeting Canadian Organizations
Canadian Cyber Centre.description:
Serial number: AV26-028
Date: October 28, 2026

Audience

This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers.

Purpose

An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested.

Details

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of an ongoing voice phishing (vishing) campaign targeting Canadian organizations, including organizations in the legal and financial sectors. Multiple Canadian firms have been targeted by individuals impersonating internal IT support and directing employees to fraudulent sign-in pages. The tradecraft and infrastructure are consistent with publicly reported operations by a financially motivated threat actor Footnote 1Footnote 2.

Throughout 2026, this activity has shifted across sectors, increasingly targeting finance and legal organizations since July Footnote 1. The Cyber Centre has identified related infrastructure naming Canadian organizations since January, with October activity concentrated on the legal sector. The campaign bypasses conventional multi-factor authentication (MFA) through real-time relay and frequently rotates lure domains, limiting the effectiveness of blocklists.

Initial Access

  • Help desk voice phishing: Callers impersonate internal IT or help desk staff and claim an urgent passkey migration, MFA enrolment or password change is required. Calls may target personal mobile phones, office phones or Microsoft Teams, and may spoof legitimate help desk numbers. Callers may reference internal IT staff or missed deadlines to add credibility and may end the call if the employee attempts independent verification Footnote 1.
  • Organisation-branded adversary-in-the-middle sign-in pages: The caller directs the employee to an organisation-branded subdomain on a generic root domain designed to mimic an enrolment portal.
    • The targeted organization’s name may appear as a subdomain of a generic domain (e.g., <org-name>.onetimesso[.]com, <org-name>.registermymfa[.]com) or be incorporated directly into a newly registered domain (e.g., <org-name>sso[.]com, <org-name>internal[.]com).
    • Domains commonly combine action words such as "activate", "enroll", "register", "create", "add", "enable", "deploy" or "set" with authentication-related terms such as "passkey", "sso", "mfa" or "2fa". Other commonly used terms include "okta", "internal", "signin", "account", "security", "portal", "setup", "connect" and "sync".
    • The page relays credentials and MFA responses to the legitimate identity provider, providing the actor with an authenticated session Footnote 1Footnote 2.

Post-Compromise Activity

After obtaining an authenticated session, the actor has been reported to Footnote 1Footnote 2:

  • Register attacker-controlled MFA methods or devices to maintain access.
  • Delete password-reset, MFA-change and security notifications, and reset passwords for non-SSO applications.
  • Use automated scripts and Microsoft Graph to access and exfiltrate data from Microsoft 365 and connected SaaS applications, including SharePoint and OneDrive.
  • Send extortion demands following data theft.

Suggested actions

The Cyber Centre recommends that organizations:

  • Deploy phishing-resistant MFA, such as FIDO2 security keys, device-bound passkeys or platform authenticators, particularly for privileged and high-risk users Footnote 3.
  • Enforce conditional access requiring managed devices and restrict sign-ins from commercial VPNs, hosting providers and residential proxies.
  • Strengthen verification for MFA resets, account recovery and new device enrolments, and reduce session lifetimesFootnote 1.
  • Monitor for suspicious MFA registrations, scripted or high-volume Microsoft 365 file access, security-email deletion and newly registered domains impersonating the organization Footnote 2.
  • Instruct employees to independently verify unexpected IT calls requesting MFA, passkey or password changes, regardless of caller ID or urgency Footnote 4.
  • Provide a clear channel for reporting suspicious calls and associated websites.
  • If compromise is suspected, revoke active sessions and tokens, reset credentials, remove unauthorized MFA methods or devices, and review mailbox and file activity.
  • Preserve relevant identity provider and Microsoft 365 audit logs for investigation Footnote 5.
  • Restrict external communications in collaboration platforms (e.g., Microsoft Teams, Webex, Slack, among others), including direct messaging, calls and meeting invitations, to trusted or operationally required external users, and regularly review guest access and permissions.

Organizations should also review the Cyber Centre’s Top 10 IT Security ActionsFootnote 6.

Should activity matching the content of this alert be discovered, recipients are encouraged to report via My Cyber Portal, or email contact@cyber.gc.ca.

Canadian Cyber Centre.title: AL26-027 - Critical vulnerability impacting Google Brotli – CVE-2026-111497
Canadian Cyber Centre.description:
Number: AL26-027
Date: October 28, 2026

Audience

This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers.

Purpose

An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested.

Details

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of a critical vulnerability affecting the Google Brotli compression libraryFootnote 1. In response to the vendor advisory, the Cyber Centre released an advisory on October 26, 2026Footnote 2.

Google Brotli is an open-source compression algorithm developed by Google that reduces the size of web content, such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, to improve website loading speed and reduce bandwidth usage.

Tracked as CVE-2026-111497Footnote 3, the vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787)Footnote 4, vulnerability affecting the Google Brotli decoder. Known as “Broccoli2Shell”Footnote 5, the vulnerability could be exploited remotely without authentication by sending specially crafted compressed data. Successful exploitation could result in memory corruption, disclosure of sensitive information, process crashes or arbitrary code execution in affected applications or services.

Because Brotli is widely integrated into other software, organizations should assess applications and products that bundle or rely on vulnerable Brotli components. Affected technologies include Node.js, Microsoft .NET, PowerShell, Bun, Envoy Proxy, Istio, and the Python Brotli and brotlicffi packages, among others.

On October 27, 2026, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026–111497 to their Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) DatabaseFootnote 6.

Suggested actions

The Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations identify affected Brotli installations and update vulnerable components to an appropriate fixed release :

Affected Product Affected versions Fixed versions
Brotli Versions 1.0.3 prior to 1.0.10 Version 1.0.10
Brotli Versions 1.1.0 prior to 1.1.1 Version 1.1.1
Brotli Versions 1.2.0 prior to 1.2.1 Version 1.2.1

The Cyber Centre recommends that organizations:

  • Identify Internet-facing systems, applications and services that use vulnerable Brotli components and prioritize their remediation, including third-party software and dependenciesFootnote 7.
  • Apply applicable security updates as soon as possible.
  • Where immediate remediation is not feasible, prevent affected applications from processing Brotli-compressed content from untrusted sources until an update can be applied.
  • Monitor affected systems for unexpected crashes, abnormal process behaviour or other suspicious activity.

Organizations should also review the Cyber Centre’s Top 10 IT Security ActionsFootnote 8.

Should activity matching the content of this alert be discovered, recipients are encouraged to report via My Cyber Portal, or email contact@cyber.gc.ca.

Canadian Cyber Centre.title: AL26-026 - Critical vulnerabilities impacting PHP - CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 - Update 2
Canadian Cyber Centre.description:
Number: AL26-026
Date: October 21, 2026
Updated: October 27, 2026

Audience

This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers.

Purpose

An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested.

Details

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of critical vulnerabilities affecting PHPFootnote 1. In response to the vendor advisory, the Cyber centre released an advisory on October 21, 2026Footnote 2.

Tracked as CVE-2026-109618Footnote 3 and CVE-2026-109619Footnote 4, these vulnerabilities are Use After Free vulnerabilities (CWE-416)Footnote 5 affecting multiple versions of PHP. Known as “php2shell”Footnote 6, successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated threat actor to execute arbitrary code on an affected system. Internet-facing PHP servers and applications are at heightened risk.

The PHP Security Team has released security updates addressing these vulnerabilities. Organizations should identify affected systems and apply the appropriate updates immediately.

PHP remains a widely deployed technology and continues to support a substantial proportion of web applications worldwide.

All PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed are at risk. PHP assess the risk as greatest for mod_php, as a demonstrated exploit allows an unauthenticated request to trigger the vulnerability before application-level code is executed.

The Cyber Centre has observed open-source reporting indicating that a Proof of Concept (PoC) is available, with no active exploitation being identified at this time, but that can change quickly.

Update 1

On October 23, 2026, the PHP Security Team published additional information regarding another remote code execution vulnerabilityFootnote 9, tracked as CVE-2026-115560Footnote 10. The vulnerability is not addressed by the security updates released on October 21, 2026.

Successful exploitation of CVE-2026-115560 requires an uncommon combination of PHP configuration and application behaviour. Applications that do not change the serialization handler at runtime are not exposed to this attack vector.

Until a security update is available, the PHP Security Team recommends disabling the session upload progress feature:
session.upload_progress.enabled=0

This mitigation was previously recommended for CVE-2026-109619. Organizations that have already applied this mitigation and kept it in place do not need to take additional action specifically for CVE-2026-115560.

Update 2

Open-source reporting indicates that CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are being exploited in the wild.

On October 26, 2026, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-109618Footnote 11 and CVE-2026-109619Footnote 12 to their Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Database.

Suggested actions

The Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations running affected PHP versions upgrade to the following fixed version:

affected PHP versions upgrade
Affected Product Affected Versions Fixed Versions
PHP 8.5.x prior to 8.5.12 8.5.12
PHP 8.4.x prior to 8.4.27 8.4.27
PHP 8.3.x prior to 8.3.36 8.3.36
PHP 8.2.x prior to 8.2.35 8.2.35

Note: versions 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details, or upgrade to a supported version.

The Cyber Centre recommends that organizations:

  • Update affected PHP installations immediately to a fixed, supported release.
  • Prioritize Internet-facing systems and applications that process untrusted input.
  • Identify third-party products, appliances and containers that include vulnerable PHP componentsFootnote 7.
  • Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied.
  • Monitor for potential compromise by reviewing web server, application, authentication, and endpoint logs for suspicious activity.
  • Investigate unexpected processes, commands, files, accounts or outbound connections associated with PHP or web-server services.
  • Continuously monitor third-party vendors for security updates, including appliances, applications and services that bundle PHP, and apply applicable patches without delay.

Organizations should also review the Cyber Centre’s Top 10 IT Security ActionsFootnote 8.

Should activity matching the content of this alert be discovered, recipients are encouraged to report via My Cyber Portal, or email contact@cyber.gc.ca.

Canadian Cyber Centre.title: AL26-025 - Critical vulnerability impacting BeyondTrust Remote Support – CVE-2026-102764
Canadian Cyber Centre.description:
Number: AL26-025
Date: October 16, 2026

Audience

This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers.

Purpose

An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested.

Details

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of a critical vulnerability affecting BeyondTrust Remote Support (RS)Footnote 1Footnote 2. In response to the vendor advisory released on October 15, 2026, the Cyber Centre released AV26-1054 on October 16, 2026Footnote 3.

Tracked as CVE-2026-102764Footnote 4, this vulnerability is an Authentication Bypass by Spoofing vulnerability (CWE-290)Footnote 5 that affects all versions of BeyondTrust Remote Support.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to exploit insufficient origin validation in internal BeyondTrust Remote Support messaging components to perform unauthorized file operations on an affected appliance without user interaction. The vulnerability requires no credentials or user action and can enable arbitrary file uploads, potentially resulting in full compromise of the appliance.

The Cyber Centre has observed open-source reporting indicating that the vulnerability is being exploited in the wildFootnote 6.

Suggested actions

The Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations running affected BeyondTrust Remote Support deployments upgrade to the following fixed version:

Affected product Affected versions Fixed versions
BeyondTrust Remote Support Versions 26.2.3 and prior BT26-05-RS patch for versions 24.3.1 to v26.2.3

BeyondTrust has confirmed that a patch addressing this vulnerability was applied to all Remote Support SaaS and Privileged Remote Access SaaS customers as of 9 October 2026. Organizations using these SaaS offerings do not need to take any additional action to remediate this issue.

The Cyber Centre also recommends organizations to:

  • identify BeyondTrust Remote Support deployments within their environments and determine whether they are SaaS-hosted or self-hosted
  • verify the installed Remote Support version. Systems running 26.2.3 or earlier are identified as affected by BeyondTrust
  • upgrade Remote Support installations older than 24.3.1 to a newer supported version before applying the remediation patch
  • apply the BT26-05-RS patch to affected self-hosted Remote Support deployments running versions 24.3.1 through 26.2.3
  • confirm automatic updates are enabled, where appropriate. BeyondTrust specifically advises manual patching for self-hosted instances that are not subscribed to automatic updates
  • as an additional defensive measure, review affected appliances for unexpected or unauthorized file activity, particularly when an appliance was exposed while vulnerable

In addition, the Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations review and implement the Cyber Centre’s Top 10 IT Security ActionsFootnote 7 with an emphasis on the following topics:

  • consolidating, monitoring, and defending Internet gateways
  • patch operating systems and applications
  • harden operating systems and applications
  • isolate web-facing applications

Should activity matching the content of this alert be discovered, recipients are encouraged to report via My Cyber Portal, or email contact@cyber.gc.ca.

Microsoft Security Update Guide.title: CVE-2026-100223 Windows NTFS Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Microsoft Security Update Guide.description:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when reparse points are created by sandboxed processes allowing sandbox escape. An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could use the sandbox escape to elevate privileges on an affected system. 

To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker would first have to log on to the system, and then run a specially crafted application to take control over the affected system.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by preventing sandboxed processes from creating reparse points targeting inaccessible files.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120350
CVE.report.description:
The Vaadin Rich Text Editor exports a video embed without escaping its value, and then parses the resulting HTML into live DOM. A value crafted to break out of the href attribute therefore runs script in the viewer's browser. An attacker who can edit shared content pastes a video embed carrying the payload, the delta is stored, and the script runs when any user opens the page, including in read only mode.

Only content persisted through asDelta() is affected. The default HTML value, set and read through setValue and getValue, is sanitized on the server with a safelist that has no iframe, so the embed does not survive that path. Vaadin 24 and older are not affected: they build the HTML value from the editor's own innerHTML, which the browser escapes.

Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include:

Product version
Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13
Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13
Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12
Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4

Mitigation
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
Upgrade to 25.2.13
Upgrade to 25.3.5

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120326
CVE.report.description:
DownloadEvent.setFileName(String) in Vaadin Flow writes the download file name into the Content-Disposition header without escaping it. When the name is pure US-ASCII the header is built as attachment; filename="<name>" with the name inserted verbatim, so a double quote in the name ends the quoted string early and the rest of the name is read by the browser as further header parameters. The inline(String) variant, present from Vaadin 25.0, builds the name the same way. An application that passes an untrusted file name to either method, for example when re-serving a file under the name it was uploaded with, lets an attacker add a filename* parameter. Browsers prefer filename* over filename, so the file is saved under a name and extension of the attacker's choosing, which defeats any file name or extension restriction the application enforces. The attacker cannot change the attachment or inline disposition itself and cannot split the header.

Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include:

Product version
Vaadin 24.8.0 - 24.8.17
Vaadin 24.9.0 - 24.9.25
Vaadin 24.10.0 - 24.10.13
Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13
Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13
Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12
Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4

Mitigation
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 24.9.26 or newer
Upgrade to 24.9.26
Upgrade to 24.10.14
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
Upgrade to 25.2.13
Upgrade to 25.3.5

Vaadin versions below 24.8 are not affected: the DownloadEvent API does not exist in them.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2022-51024

Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-18.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2022-51023

Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2022-51022

Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-20.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2022-51021

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-120350 - Stored Cross-Site Scripting in the Vaadin Rich Text Editor via an Unescaped Video Embed
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-120350
Published : Nov. 10, 2026, 11:50 a.m. | 21 minutes ago
Description :The Vaadin Rich Text Editor exports a video embed without escaping its value, and then parses the resulting HTML into live DOM. A value crafted to break out of the href attribute therefore runs script in the viewer's browser. An attacker who can edit shared content pastes a video embed carrying the payload, the delta is stored, and the script runs when any user opens the page, including in read only mode. Only content persisted through asDelta() is affected. The default HTML value, set and read through setValue and getValue, is sanitized on the server with a safelist that has no iframe, so the embed does not survive that path. Vaadin 24 and older are not affected: they build the HTML value from the editor's own innerHTML, which the browser escapes. Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include: Product version Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13 Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13 Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12 Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4 Mitigation No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer Upgrade to 25.2.13 Upgrade to 25.3.5

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-120326 - Unescaped Download File Name Allows Content-Disposition Parameter Injection in Vaadin Flow
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-120326
Published : Nov. 10, 2026, 11:49 a.m. | 22 minutes ago
Description :DownloadEvent.setFileName(String) in Vaadin Flow writes the download file name into the Content-Disposition header without escaping it. When the name is pure US-ASCII the header is built as attachment; filename="" with the name inserted verbatim, so a double quote in the name ends the quoted string early and the rest of the name is read by the browser as further header parameters. The inline(String) variant, present from Vaadin 25.0, builds the name the same way. An application that passes an untrusted file name to either method, for example when re-serving a file under the name it was uploaded with, lets an attacker add a filename* parameter. Browsers prefer filename* over filename, so the file is saved under a name and extension of the attacker's choosing, which defeats any file name or extension restriction the application enforces. The attacker cannot change the attachment or inline disposition itself and cannot split the header. Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include: Product version Vaadin 24.8.0 - 24.8.17 Vaadin 24.9.0 - 24.9.25 Vaadin 24.10.0 - 24.10.13 Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13 Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13 Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12 Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4 Mitigation No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 24.9.26 or newer Upgrade to 24.9.26 Upgrade to 24.10.14 No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer Upgrade to 25.2.13 Upgrade to 25.3.5 Vaadin versions below 24.8 are not affected: the DownloadEvent API does not exist in them.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-120999 - Improper authentication lets Google sign-in and confirmation links sign users in to accounts registered with their email address by someone else
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-120999
Published : Nov. 10, 2026, 11:16 a.m. | 55 minutes ago
Description :Improper Authentication vulnerability in Google sign-in and email confirmation in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an attacker who registers another person's email address to share that person's account once they sign in. NervesHub.Accounts.update_or_create_user_from_ueberauth/1 signs a Google user in to any account carrying the same email that is not yet linked to a Google account, links it and marks the email confirmed, without the account's owner ever having proved they own the address. NervesHubWeb.SessionController.confirm/2 likewise signs in whoever follows a confirmation link. An attacker registers the address from the sign-up form, changes their own account's email to it, or registers it as an organization admin from an invite link, and keeps the password; when the address's owner signs in with Google or follows the confirmation link, they land in that account. The Google path also creates accounts with registrations closed and never checks Google's email_verified claim, and the API's password sign-in in NervesHubWeb.API.UserController issues tokens to accounts whose email was never confirmed. The attacker gains only what the victim is granted afterwards, and nothing on accounts whose owners never use either path. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.3.0 before 2.5.3.
Severity: 7.4 | HIGH

cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-63634
Published : Nov. 9, 2026, 8:59 p.m. | 34 minutes ago
Description :pympp is a Python SDK for the Machine Payments Protocol. Prior to version 0.9.1, when the server acts as the fee_payer, pympp validates calldata using eth_abi decoding, which is lenient about trailing bytes. The FeePayerPolicy caps gas_limit (≤ 2 M) and max_fee_per_gas (≤ 100 Gwei) but does not check calldata length. Tempo uses legacy calldata gas pricing: 16 gas per non-zero byte. Appending N bytes of 0x01 padding inflates actual gas used by N × 16 while keeping gas_limit and max_fee_per_gas within policy caps. The server cosigns and broadcasts the padded transaction, draining its fee-payer wallet. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.1.

Description :Nuxt UI is an intuitive Vue UI library powered by Reka UI and Tailwind CSS. Prior to 4.8.1, the server-rendered form element produced by UForm in src/runtime/components/Form.vue omits the method and action attributes and relies solely on the hydrated @submit.prevent handler to stop native submission. UAuthForm composes UForm and can render named credential fields, including an input with type password, inside the same markup. If a user submits before Vue hydration completes, or when the client bundle is blocked or unavailable, the browser performs its default GET submission and serializes the named fields into the current URL query string. The credentials can then appear in the address bar, browser history, reverse-proxy, CDN, or WAF request logs, and Referer headers sent with same-origin subresource requests. This issue is fixed in version 4.8.1.

Description :Signal K Server is a server application that runs on a central hub in a boat. From 2.0.0 until 2.34.0 for Signal K Server and from 1.0.0 until 1.5.3 for @signalk/resources-provider, the v2 REST route GET /signalk/v2/api/resources/:resourceType/:resourceId accepts an unsafe resourceId that can escape the intended resource directory. The route passes the attacker-controlled resourceId through src/api/resources/index.ts to FileStore.getResource() in packages/resources-provider-plugin/src/filestorage.ts without adequate path containment, allowing arbitrary JSON files reachable by the server to be read. Related PUT and DELETE resource operations can write or delete files outside the storage root. Deployments with allow_readonly enabled permit anonymous reads, while other deployments require a readonly user token. cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:

Published : Nov. 10, 2026, 6:38 p.m. | 29 minutes ago
Description :HarnessRouter is a self-hosted unified API for running agent harnesses with sessions, streaming, files, cancellation, and failure handling. Prior to 0.31.8, a console that is not in self-hosted mode attaches the server's internal key to requests carrying an Authorization header before validating the bearer, while the service-only PUT and GET /v1/orgs/{org}/connections/{name}, PUT /v1/orgs/{org}/policy/{backend}, and /internal/* routes trust that key and take the organization from the URL. In a multi-organization deployment, a remote caller can use a made-up bearer to rewrite another organization's provider connection to an attacker-controlled endpoint, causing later prompts to be disclosed and attacker-controlled responses to influence tasks. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.8.

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-120730 - Mass assignment of organization, product and deployment group IDs allows users to write into other organizations and receive their firmware
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-120730
Published : Nov. 10, 2026, 11:16 a.m. | 50 minutes ago
Description :Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes vulnerability in the device API, device forms, signing key and product forms and JITP settings in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user who manages devices in any organization to write into other organizations via submitted org_id, product_id and deployment_id fields. The device API create and update actions and the dashboard device forms pass the request parameters to NervesHub.Devices.Device.changeset/2, which casts the organization, product, deployment group and update state as given. The signing key and product forms merge the session's organization into the submitted parameters so that a submitted org_id wins, and the JITP changeset accepts any product_id. Each request requires the manage role only in the user's own organization, and any account can create one. A device placed on another organization's deployment group, or moved into its product, is sent that organization's firmware with a download URL. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization, and cannot upload firmware to it. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-119446 - Session fixation in the CLI login flow allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain a user's API token
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-119446
Published : Nov. 10, 2026, 11:16 a.m. | 50 minutes ago
Description :Session Fixation vulnerability in the CLI login flow in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain an API token for another user's account via a crafted login link. Starting a CLI login with POST /api/auth/cli_session needs no authentication and returns a polling token, a confirmation URL that carries that token, and a confirmation code. When a signed-in user opens that URL and clicks Confirm, NervesHub.Accounts.verify_cli_session_token/2 creates an API token for the user's account and stores it on the login, and the next poll of GET /api/auth/cli_session/ returns it to whoever started the login. The confirmation code is only displayed and is never compared with anything, so it cannot show that the person confirming is the one who started the login. The confirm form carries a CSRF token and the page cannot be framed, so the attacker has to persuade the user to open the link and click the button themselves. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.5.0 before 2.5.3.

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-76877 - WPML Multilingual CMS <= 4.9.7 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass in Language-per-Domain SSO via 'wpml_sso_token_domain' Parameter
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-76877
Published : Nov. 10, 2026, 7:16 a.m. | 4 hours, 50 minutes ago
Description :The WPML Multilingual CMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Race Condition in versions up to, and including, 4.9.7. This is due to the `process_iframe_request` function's language-per-domain SSO handler generating the cross-domain sign-in token via `wp_create_nonce('wpml_sso')` on the logout landing page, where the browser has already discarded its authentication cookies — so `wp_get_session_token()` returns an empty string and the token collapses to the shared anonymous nonce for the current 12-hour tick rather than a user-bound secret — and then storing it in the `wpml_sso_user__` transient mapped to the victim's `user_id` with no binding to the specific sign-out action or requesting client. Because an unauthenticated attacker can independently derive the identical token by triggering the logout confirmation flow on `wp-login.php?action=logout`, and because the `is_iframe_request()` gate conditions (the per-domain SSO `started` transient and domain-hash derived from the public constant `SSO_NONCE`) are fully computable within the 60-second `SSO_TIMEOUT` window, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the forged `wpml_sso_token_domain` parameter with a `wpml_user_signed_in` status to a secondary language-domain endpoint before the legitimate `wpml_user_signed_out` iframe fires, causing WordPress authentication cookies to be issued for the victim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to gain access to accounts of users — including administrators — who are actively in the process of logging out during the race window.
Severity: 8.1 | HIGH

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: WordPress Core Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition Vulnerability
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-119977 is a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition (CWE-367) in WordPress Core that affects the full-package core upgrade process. During an update, WordPress stages upgrade files in a predictable, web-accessible directory under `wp-content/upgrade/`. These files include the `setup-config.php` installer.

An unauthenticated remote attacker who accesses the staged installer during the upgrade window can exploit this condition to execute arbitrary code on the server. According to published technical analyses, the attacker can supply their own database configuration details, causing the upgrade process to overwrite the site's existing `wp-config.php` file with the attacker's configuration. This can allow the attacker to create an administrator account and execute arbitrary PHP code.

The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 8.1. Exploitation requires no authentication or user interaction but is timing-dependent, as the attack is only possible while a vulnerable site is actively performing a full-package core update.

Although the exploitation window is limited to the duration of the update process, the exposure is significant because WordPress sites are widely deployed and internet-facing. Organizations running affected versions should prioritize applying the security update and verify that no unauthorized changes or administrator accounts were introduced during potentially vulnerable upgrade windows.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Fixed versions: WordPress released 7.1.4 on October 28, 2026, with fixes for each supported branch.

1. Block web access to wp-content/upgrade/ before updating. The first update to a fixed release still runs through the vulnerable updater. Researchers recommend denying the path at the web server (Nginx or Apache) and confirming a 403 response before starting the update.
2. Apply the security update. Upgrade to WordPress 7.1.4, or to the fixed release for your branch, then verify the installed version.
3. Clean up staging files. Delete leftover files under wp-content/upgrade/ that the updater did not remove.
4. Monitor for exploitation attempts. Review web server logs for requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade/, especially setup-config.php.
5. Review for compromise indicators. Check wp-config.php for unexpected changes, such as a different database host. Look for unfamiliar administrator accounts, unknown plugins, and unrecognized PHP files.
6. If compromise is suspected, restore a known-good configuration, rotate database and administrator credentials, and engage incident response.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor exploitation attempts targeting WordPress Core and the associated attack techniques.

FortiGuard customers should use multiple layers of defense to help identify and mitigate suspicious activity associated with the exploitation of CVE-2026-119977:
- FortiGate Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): Provides network-level intrusion prevention and detection against known exploitation attempts targeting WordPress Core vulnerabilities. https://www.fortiguard.com/encyclopedia/ips/62806
- FortiEDR: Behavioral detection capabilities can help identify suspicious PHP execution, command execution, and other post-exploitation activity on monitored endpoints.
- FortiGuard Incident Response: Organizations suspecting compromise can engage FortiGuard Incident Response for investigation, containment, and remediation.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: OT Refrigeration Control Systems Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

November 9, 2026 Update – Threat Attribution: On November 9, 2026, France's CERT-FR published a threat intelligence report attributing the October 11–12 attacks against industrial refrigeration controllers to Shahid Kaveh, an Iranian cyber-offensive unit operating within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Electronic and Cyber Center (IRGC-CEC). According to the report, the attack compromised refrigeration controllers at approximately 700 retail locations across France, modifying defrost settings to trigger high-temperature cycles, resulting in significant product losses and at least 15 reported fires. The assessment is supported by shared attack infrastructure, the use of the FOFA scanning tool, promotion of the operation through the group's CyberbanNews channel, and traces of Persian language in the attack infrastructure. CERT-FR also documents the group's broader targeting of industrial control systems, including Schneider Electric, Siemens, and Rockwell equipment, and its historical use of Modbus over TCP port 502 for industrial reconnaissance.

November 2, 2026 Update: A new wave of suspected cyberattacks has affected supermarket refrigeration systems across several European countries, including Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia. Reported incidents involved attackers manipulating refrigeration controls and triggering defrost cycles or raising temperatures, with some equipment reportedly reaching 50°C. Affected retailers include ICA, Coop, Carrefour, Delhaize, Colruyt, and SuperValu. Sweden's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-SE) confirmed it was responding to incidents involving ICA and Coop stores. However, authorities have not established whether these incidents are connected to the October attacks in France or share the same threat actors or infrastructure. No threat group has claimed responsibility, and no new malware or indicators of compromise have been publicly confirmed.

On October 11–12, 2026, attackers compromised refrigeration control systems at supermarkets across France, remotely manipulating refrigeration settings and triggering defrost cycles. The attacks caused temperatures in some refrigeration units to rise to as high as 50°C, resulting in food spoilage and operational disruption. Affected retailers reportedly included Intermarché, Netto, Carrefour, Coopérative U, Monoprix, and E.Leclerc.

France's national cybersecurity agency, CERT-FR, reported compromises involving Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers, as well as Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. These systems monitor and manage commercial refrigeration and related building operations. Their compromise can allow unauthorized changes to operating parameters, potentially disrupting temperature control and damaging perishable goods.

Separate research by Claroty Team82 identified vulnerabilities affecting Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers, including:
CVE-2025-41450, an authentication bypass
CVE-2025-41451, an OS command injection vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution
CVE-2025-41452, a web server configuration vulnerability that can lead to denial of service
Danfoss released fixes for the above vulnerabilities, and organizations should update affected devices to the applicable patched firmware.

Additional research by Claroty Team82 and CISA documented vulnerabilities affecting Copeland XWEB Pro controllers, including:
CVE-2026-25085, an authentication bypass
CVE-2026-21718, an authentication bypass that can enable pre-authentication code execution
CVE-2026-24663, an unauthenticated OS command injection vulnerability
The affected Copeland models include XWEB300D PRO, XWEB500D PRO, and XWEB500B PRO running firmware version 1.12.1 or earlier. Organizations should consult the vendor's remediation guidance and apply the appropriate firmware updates.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

On October 12, France's national cybersecurity response team, CERT-FR, issued alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 warning of numerous compromises involving remote refrigeration controllers.

Organizations should immediately remove direct internet exposure from refrigeration controllers and restrict remote administration to secure VPN connections or protected management networks. Review controller configurations, particularly temperature settings and defrost schedules, and apply available firmware updates and vendor-recommended security settings. Change default credentials and replace unsupported, end-of-life devices where necessary.

If compromise is suspected, isolate affected equipment and follow vendor and CERT-FR recovery guidance before restoring operations. A factory reset alone is insufficient if the device remains vulnerable and exposed. Organizations should also segment OT networks from corporate IT environments, restrict access to authorized personnel, and monitor for unexpected changes to refrigeration settings.

Danfoss identifies firmware R4.2 as the fix for CVE-2025-41450 and R4.3.1 as the fix for CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452. Verify the correct release against the specific device model.

• FortiGuard OT Vulnerability Protection – Detects and blocks network-based attacks targeting industrial services and protocols covered by available OT signatures.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Linux Kernel Remote Code Execution
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-98432, a critical use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 networking subsystem that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with kernel-level privileges.

The vulnerability stems from improper memory management during TCP connection request processing. Under specific conditions, concurrent operations may access socket-option memory after it has been freed, resulting in a use-after-free condition.

An attacker can potentially trigger this flaw by sending specially crafted IPv4 TCP packets containing IP options to a vulnerable system. Exploitation requires precise timing but does not require authentication or user interaction.

Successful exploitation could result in kernel memory corruption, information disclosure, denial of service, or potentially remote code execution with kernel-level privileges.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The vulnerability was introduced in Linux kernel 4.4. The upstream Linux kernel CVE team has published fixes for multiple supported kernel branches.

Ubuntu confirmed on November 2 that fixes for Ubuntu 22.04 and newer were available in its proposed repository while undergoing qualification testing. Ubuntu 26.10 already includes the fix.

Organizations running potentially affected Linux systems should:
1. Apply security updates: Install the latest kernel security updates provided by the respective Linux distribution.
2. Reboot affected systems: Restart systems after installing the updated kernel to ensure the patched kernel is running.
3. Restrict network exposure: Limit unnecessary inbound TCP connections from untrusted networks.
4. Filter IPv4 packets containing IP options: Red Hat provides an interim nftables rule to reduce exposure to the vulnerable code path.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor CVE-2026-98432, including developments in exploitation research, vendor security updates, and the availability of security patches across affected Linux distributions.

• FortiGuard Labs will provide additional updates as new intelligence and protections become available.

• FortiGate Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): Provides network-level intrusion prevention and detection against known exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2026-98432. Intrusion Prevention | FortiGuard Labs

• FortiGuard Labs has released a Virtual Patch signature (10010015) to protect vulnerable systems against exploitation of CVE-2026-98432. The signature provides protection at the network layer, helping prevent exploitation attempts without requiring immediate changes to the underlying Linux kernel. FortiGuard Virtual Patching Service | FortiGuard Labs

• FortiGuard Labs has released Endpoint Vulnerability signatures to identify vulnerable Linux kernel components across your network, helping organizations detect potentially affected systems and prioritize remediation. FortiGuard Labs

• FortiGuard Incident Response supports investigation, containment, and recovery following suspected compromise of Linux distributions.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Day Exploitation
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

FortiGuard Labs is monitoring active exploitation of multiple zero-day vulnerabilities affecting Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS), an enterprise remote access VPN solution. Threat actors have chained three vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357, and CVE-2026-118527) to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution on vulnerable appliances.

According to security researchers, the attacks have been observed since at least October 1, 2026. The activity was initially attributed to a previously unidentified threat actor tracked by Volexity as UTA0576.

The attack chain begins with CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute commands without authentication. Attackers then leverage CVE-2026-111357 to escalate privileges and CVE-2026-118527 to upload attacker-controlled files to predetermined locations on the appliance.

Once access is obtained, observed post-exploitation activities include credential theft, Active Directory reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and network scanning. Researchers also reported attempts to retrieve Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) credentials and BitLocker recovery keys.

Notably, the attackers reportedly deployed no malware or web shells. Instead, they re-exploited the appliance to execute individual commands and manipulated system logs to conceal their activity and evade Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool.

Ivanti confirmed that exploitation affected a limited number of customers before disclosure. CISA has now added all three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Ivanti Connect Secure appliances running the following versions are affected:
- Version 25.1.1.2 and earlier.
- Version 25.1.2.2 and earlier.
- Version 22.8R2.5 and earlier.

Organizations using Ivanti Connect Secure should immediately apply the latest available security updates.

Recommended actions:
- Upgrade Ivanti Connect Secure to a fixed release. Versions 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 address the two additional vulnerabilities. Organizations should follow Ivanti's current upgrade guidance for their specific release branch. Do not assume that installing the earlier October update for CVE-2026-104935 provides complete protection. The subsequent vulnerabilities require additional updates.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Node.js Brotli Remote Code Execution (Node2Shell)
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Google Brotli decoder, a component used to decompress data encoded with the Brotli compression algorithm. Brotli is widely used in web communications and is bundled with Node.js through its `zlib` module.

Brotli is an open-source project developed and maintained by Google for lossless data compression. It shrinks files so they can be transmitted faster without affecting the original data.

The vulnerability occurs when the decoder processes specially crafted Brotli-compressed input. An attacker who can supply malicious compressed data to a vulnerable application may corrupt adjacent memory, potentially leading to information disclosure, denial of service, or remote code execution.

The root cause is an error in the decoder's handling of malformed block-switch commands. Under certain conditions, the streaming decoder incorrectly treats an invalid block switch as a request for additional input rather than a format error. This can cause data to be written beyond the bounds of an internal eight-byte buffer, corrupting adjacent process memory.

The vulnerability affects Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. Fixed versions include 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1, depending on the release branch. The Node.js project has also released patched versions for affected release lines.

On October 22, 2026, Imperva published research demonstrating remote code execution against a vulnerable Node.js build. Public proof-of-concept references are also listed in Red Hat's vulnerability bulletin, increasing the risk to unpatched deployments.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations should prioritize updating vulnerable Node.js deployments and Brotli libraries to fixed versions. Because the vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, systems that process untrusted compressed content should receive particular attention.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply security updates: Upgrade Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1, or 26.12.1, as appropriate, or a later fixed release. Update standalone Brotli packages to the applicable fixed version.
2. Review application exposure: Identify services that decompress untrusted Brotli data, including applications using node:zlib, HTTP clients processing compressed responses, and middleware that decompresses incoming request bodies.
3. Apply temporary restrictions where feasible: Until updates are deployed, limit untrusted Brotli-compressed traffic on affected application paths where operationally practical. Test any restrictions to avoid disrupting legitimate traffic.
4. Investigate suspicious activity: Review application and process logs for unexpected crashes or decompression errors. Correlate anomalies with incoming traffic and runtime versions; these symptoms alone do not confirm exploitation.
5. Rebuild and redeploy affected containers: Ensure production images and bundled dependencies include the patched runtime or library rather than relying solely on host-level updates.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-111497 and will update this Threat Signal as new threat intelligence and protection information become available. Organizations should prioritize patching affected Node.js deployments and Brotli libraries, particularly where applications process untrusted compressed data.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP, a widely used server-side scripting language that powers websites and web applications. They involve flaws in PHP's internal request-processing and memory-management behavior that can be triggered when handling malicious requests. Both are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities rated as 9.2 (CVSS 4.0).

• CVE-2026-109618 - RCE via out-of-memory corruption: An out-of-memory condition can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Subsequent request-cleanup operations may incorrectly process this invalid data, potentially enabling remote code execution.

• CVE-2026-109619 - RCE via stale global state: Internal request state can persist after its associated memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may access this stale state before normal initialization resets it, potentially enabling remote code execution.

Successful exploitation could compromise the PHP application process and potentially provide access to sensitive server resources, application data, or databases, depending on the permissions of the affected process and the surrounding environment.

PHP announced emergency security updates for October 21, 2026, following reports that details of the vulnerabilities had leaked ahead of the planned disclosure. Subsequent reports highlighted ongoing exploit research and potential attack activity, underscoring the urgency of applying the available patches. However, widespread exploitation of either vulnerability has not been independently confirmed.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP installations that process web requests, including deployments using PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. PHP identifies Apache deployments using mod_php as particularly at risk because a demonstrated exploit can trigger before application code runs.

Organizations should prioritize patching internet-facing PHP servers and other exposed deployments immediately.
1. Apply the security updates. Upgrade to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, as appropriate. Organizations using vendor-maintained packages should apply the corresponding security updates from their distributions or service providers.
2. Reduce exposure until patching is complete. Where immediate remediation is not possible, isolate affected systems from untrusted networks or temporarily disable exposed services when operationally feasible.
3. Review request-processing limits. Apply appropriate web-server or reverse-proxy limits for request sizes, input fields, multipart sections, headers, and nesting depth. These controls can reduce exposure but are not a substitute for patching.
4. Review potentially vulnerable systems. Investigate suspicious web requests, unexpected PHP worker behavior, unexplained process execution, and unusual access to application files or databases. Prioritize internet-facing systems and investigate potential compromise before returning affected services to production.

PHP 8.1 and older are no longer supported by the PHP project and do not receive its standard security updates. Organizations using these versions should check whether their operating-system vendor provides backported fixes or migrate to a supported release.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs recommends a defense-in-depth approach to reduce exposure to attacks targeting vulnerable PHP deployments and is currently monitoring the situation and will provide updates as new information becomes available and additional protections are released.

• FortiGuard Labs has released IPS signatures to detect and protect against attacks CVE-2026-109619, CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-115560. [IPS version 37.317]

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Trimble Cityworks Remote Code Execution Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

Trimble Cityworks contains a deserialization vulnerability. This could allow an authenticated user to perform a remote code execution attack against a customer's Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) web server, potentially resulting in downtime and potential loss of service.

According to Trimble Cityworks website, it provides a Geographic Information System (GIS)-centric solution for local governments, utilities, airports, and public works agencies to manage and maintain infrastructure across the full lifecycle.

Trimble has investigated customer reports of hackers exploiting the vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to networks, confirming that active exploitation is occurring. CISA has added CVE-2025-0994 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog on February 7, 2025, based on the evidence of active exploitation.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

• The CVE-2025-0994 flaw impacts Cityworks versions prior to 15.8.9 and Cityworks with office companion versions before 23.10.
• Trimble has released updates addressing this deserialization flaw. Ensure these updates are applied to your systems.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Atlassian Arbitrary File Access Vulnerability
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack? CVE-2026-21589 is a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability affecting multiple Atlassian Data Center and Server products. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within an affected application's web root, provided the attacker knows the exact file path and name.

The vulnerability stems from improper restrictions on access to files within the web application root. Successful exploitation could expose sensitive files and potentially provide information useful for further attacks, depending on the affected application's configuration and the files accessible.

The vulnerability requires no authentication or user interaction, making internet-facing deployments a priority for remediation.
What is the recommended Mitigation? Atlassian published its security advisory on October 5, 2026, and recommends immediate remediation for affected installations. Atlassian recommends that you patch each of your affected installations to fixed versions or the latest version.

Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.title: Linux kernel RCE CVE-2026-98432
Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 9.8

CVE-2026-98432:ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it. Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req(). tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice. Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop() calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed. Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in ip_options_build(). A similar issue exists with request socket migration (net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK, or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree(). Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt (do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well. IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This will be addressed in a separate patch.

CVE-2026-109618PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory.CVE-2026-109619PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized.CVE-2026-115560PHP has published a security warning regarding an unpatched RCE vulnerability in session upload progress.No Fortinet product meets the conditions required for exploitation.
